tasks.short: Recommend bargaining objectives, options and a negotiating mandate.

steps.what: Review current agreements, previous settlements and outstanding workforce concerns.

loop.input: Approved agreements, settlements and recorded concerns.
loop.output: Agreement brief with clause references and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Verify document versions and source references; specialist checks interpretation and omissions.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass; unresolved clauses go to the specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates cannot extract varied clauses and concerns from free text.

steps.what: Collect workforce totals, pay costs and budget limits.
Discuss priorities, constraints and acceptable trade-offs with management and workforce representatives.
Compare the costs and coverage of bargaining options.
Draft recommended objectives, fallback positions and escalation limits.

loop.input: Reviewed priorities, scenarios and risk assessment.
loop.output: Mandate proposal with options, trade-offs and source references.
loop.check: Specialist checks recommendations; costs must match approved scenario calculations.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unsupported recommendations remain marked for human completion.
loop.why_not_simpler: Explaining competing priorities requires contextual writing beyond a fixed template.

steps.what: Challenge the recommendation and approve the negotiating mandate.

tasks.design: A controlled workspace in {DOCS} assembles agreement material, while an integration reads aggregate baselines from {HCM}, {PAYROLL} and {ERP}. Deterministic calculations produce bargaining scenarios; bounded extraction and drafting produce referenced briefs and a mandate proposal. The specialist leads priority discussions, and the HR manager approves the negotiating mandate.
tasks.previous_blocker: Agreement interpretation, scattered evidence and changing negotiation priorities made a complete automated recommendation impractical.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding can shorten delivery of integrations and scenario tools. Bounded models can prepare referenced drafts, with no assumed breakthrough in bargaining judgement.
tasks.still_hard: Understanding trust, informal commitments and sector constraints remains difficult. National rules and bargaining authority differ across employers.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising which trade-offs people can accept, protecting credibility and deciding when a concession is worth making.

ambition.what: Reassess the fallback position after each material change in bargaining demands.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time assembling evidence and more time testing options with stakeholders. They can initiate scenario reviews; authority to approve the mandate remains with management.

reach.task: Estimate the recurring cost and distribution of proposed pay changes.
reach.learn: Pay structures, employer on-costs, eligibility rules and recurring versus one-off costs.

evidence.claim: Referenced drafting and deterministic scenario calculations are plausible building blocks; the digest supplies no labor-relations implementation case.
Generated reports need source verification because fabricated references have caused a documented failure.
Dutch national rules include works-council consent rights for specified employee-data and monitoring arrangements.

assumptions: The employer bargains locally or prepares positions within a sector agreement.
Time shares and build ranges are estimates for a mid-size European employer, not measured findings.
Most bargaining effort remains discussion and judgement, consistent with the supplied priors.
The design uses aggregate workforce information where possible and excludes individual bargaining profiles.
unknowns: Which agreements apply and who can approve the mandate.
Whether workforce representatives can receive the proposed briefing material.
Available exports, access rights and baseline data quality.
Applicable national consultation requirements and existing employee-data arrangements.
research_questions: Can each scenario reproduce a previous settlement's actual cost?
How much drafting time remains after specialists verify every material clause reference?
What GDPR lawful basis, special-category conditions and national consultation steps apply to the intended data?
new_work: Review extracted clauses and proposed narrative.
Maintain scenario formulas, eligibility rules and agreement versions.
Resolve missing baseline data and integration failures.
Maintain restricted access and retention settings.

tasks.short: Check adherence to labor agreements and resolve potential departures.

steps.what: Translate agreement clauses into checks, evidence requirements and review dates.

loop.output: Proposed checklist with clauses, effective dates, evidence and ambiguous obligations.
loop.check: Specialist approves every interpretation and executable rule before activation.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass; ambiguous clauses remain manual checks.
loop.why_not_simpler: Agreements express obligations in varied prose; literal matching misses qualifications.

steps.what: Retrieve pay, hours, absence and staffing evidence for the review period.
Compare recorded practice against measurable agreement requirements.
Investigate exceptions and obligations that require contextual interpretation.
Discuss findings and disputed interpretations with managers and workforce representatives.
Approve corrective actions or escalate unresolved interpretations.
Update the action register and remind responsible teams about deadlines.

tasks.design: A reviewed control checklist in {DOCS} drives scheduled checks on permitted {HCM} and {PAYROLL} data through {DATA_PLATFORM}. A restricted {WORKFLOW} register holds evidence, exceptions and approved remediation, with internal reminders and a status view. People investigate context, discuss contested findings and approve corrective actions before affected teams execute them.
tasks.previous_blocker: Agreement clauses were not executable rules, and evidence crossed records, documents and local interpretations.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing exports and workflow features can support routine controls. AI coding reduces the effort of joining records and building checks; a bounded model only proposes clause extraction.
tasks.still_hard: Retroactive changes, local exceptions and ambiguous entitlements need careful interpretation. A detected mismatch is not proof of misconduct or non-compliance.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguishing administrative errors from substantive breaches and resolving disputed interpretations fairly.

ambition.what: Review emerging agreement exceptions each pay cycle.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time reconciling records and more time resolving exceptions before they recur. They can prioritise investigations; disciplinary and pay decisions retain their existing approval rights.

reach.task: Trace and correct an agreement-related pay discrepancy.
reach.learn: Pay codes, retrospective adjustments, effective dates and payroll cut-offs.

evidence.claim: Deterministic controls can compare structured records with approved agreement rules; no direct implementation case is supplied.
GDPR Article 22 restricts solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects.
The Dutch supervisory list identifies employee-monitoring processing requiring a DPIA.
The EU AI Act identifies specified employment and worker-management AI uses as high-risk.

assumptions: Existing system records contain enough evidence for a useful subset of agreement checks.
Checks flag discrepancies and missing evidence; they do not score worker conduct or determine entitlements.
Document review and discussion remain substantial, while measurable reconciliation supports more automation than the overall task prior suggests.
Build ranges include a pilot across historical pay periods.
unknowns: Which obligations are measurable from existing records.
Whether time records are available through the {HCM} or require another source.
The quality of effective dates, worker categories and local exceptions.
Existing GDPR assessments, access restrictions and national consultation arrangements.
research_questions: Which checks reproduce confirmed historical discrepancies without excessive false alarms?
Does the proposed use constitute employee monitoring or high-risk worker-management AI?
Which controls can be configured in existing systems before custom code is needed?
new_work: Approve and version control rules when agreements change.
Investigate false positives and missing evidence.
Reconcile source totals and monitor integration failures.
Review access, retention and the continued necessity of each data field.

tasks.short: Meet interested parties to discuss negotiations, grievances and other labor relations matters.

steps.what: Review the matter, relevant clauses and previous correspondence.

loop.output: Case brief separating recorded facts, allegations, positions and unanswered questions.
loop.check: Specialist verifies chronology, references, representation rights and omitted counter-evidence.
loop.stop: One summary and one correction pass; contradictions remain explicit for human review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text correspondence contains conflicting accounts that fixed fields cannot summarise adequately.

steps.what: Arrange participants, availability and practical meeting requirements.
Prepare the agenda, evidence pack and mandate reminders.
Hear concerns, clarify positions and explore possible resolutions within the mandate.
Approve proposed commitments that exceed the specialist's existing mandate.
Prepare and circulate the checked meeting record, positions and next actions.

loop.input: Specialist's written notes and approved positions.
loop.output: Meeting record distinguishing agreed points, proposals, disagreements and assigned actions.
loop.check: Specialist verifies wording and disclosure scope before circulation; disputed points remain marked.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unclear commitments require human clarification.
loop.why_not_simpler: Written notes require contextual phrasing to avoid presenting tentative proposals as agreements.

tasks.design: Configured {CALENDAR} and {EMAIL} flows arrange meetings using approved participants and neutral invitations. A bounded model prepares a referenced case brief in {DOCS}; deterministic templates assemble the meeting pack, and a second bounded drafting step prepares minutes from written notes. People conduct the conversation, approve concessions and check every circulated record.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sensitive conversations depend on trust, representation and context. Preparation and records were often bundled with the meeting itself.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing scheduling features and simple document assembly cover routine coordination. Bounded reading and drafting can reduce preparation work without replacing the conversation.
tasks.still_hard: Contested facts, accessibility needs, representation rights and careful wording of commitments remain demanding. Participants may disagree about the meeting record.
tasks.human_edge: Listening, building trust, managing conflict and knowing when to pause or seek a different resolution.

ambition.what: Offer an early facilitated conversation before a concern becomes a formal grievance.

tasks.altitude: More of the specialist's week becomes available for direct conversations and follow-up. They can offer earlier intervention within existing authority; settlement rights do not automatically expand.

reach.task: Identify when a grievance needs a specialist discrimination response.
reach.learn: Protected grounds, impartial intake, reasonable adjustments and escalation routes.

evidence.claim: Scheduling and document assembly are feasible support tools; bargaining and grievance conversations remain human work.
The EU AI Act prohibits workplace emotion recognition, subject to its specified exceptions.
Source checking matters when generated text could introduce unsupported statements.

assumptions: The steps represent a typical substantive meeting; approval is needed only when proposals exceed the mandate.
Routine scheduling uses an approved participant list and reveals no grievance details in invitations.
The design uses written notes and does not require recording or emotion analysis.
The supplied low automation prior fits the conversation itself; preparation and paperwork offer a larger gain.
unknowns: Who may attend, represent a party or approve commitments.
Which cases require separate investigation or legal involvement.
Existing rules for sharing records and correcting disputed minutes.
research_questions: Which preparation documents can be reused without exposing another case's information?
Can participants distinguish proposals from agreements in the generated meeting record?
What GDPR and national rules govern case access, representative information and retention?
new_work: Check briefs for missing counter-evidence and incorrect chronology.
Review disclosure scope before sharing packs or minutes.
Resolve participant corrections and disputed records.
Maintain invitation templates, participant permissions and agenda templates.

tasks.short: Assess the legal, financial, operational and relationship risks of bargaining strategies.

steps.what: Assemble bargaining options, workforce totals and operational dependencies.
Review agreement constraints, previous disputes and relevant legal advice.

loop.input: Approved agreements, dispute records and legal advice authorised for processing.
loop.output: Referenced constraints, relevant precedents and unresolved legal questions.
loop.check: Specialist verifies applicability, dates and source passages; legal adviser resolves legal uncertainty.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass; missing authority or conflicting advice is escalated.
loop.why_not_simpler: Constraints and qualifications are embedded in varied narrative documents.

steps.what: Calculate financial exposure and operational impacts under explicit scenarios.
Challenge assumptions about workforce response, operational resilience and possible mitigations.
Draft a comparative risk assessment with uncertainties and mitigation choices.

loop.input: Reviewed calculations, constraints, assumptions and mitigation options.
loop.output: Comparative assessment separating calculated exposure from human judgements and unknowns.
loop.check: Specialist checks all figures and references; no invented likelihoods or unsupported legal conclusions.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unresolved risks remain explicit rather than receiving invented ratings.
loop.why_not_simpler: Explaining interacting risks and uncertainty requires contextual writing.

steps.what: Agree risk ratings, acceptable exposure and escalation triggers.

tasks.design: A restricted {DATA_PLATFORM} job assembles approved evidence from {HCM}, {ERP} and {DOCS}; deterministic calculations expose the consequences of explicit bargaining scenarios. Bounded extraction and drafting create referenced constraints and a comparative assessment in {DOCS}. People validate behavioural assumptions, resolve legal uncertainty and approve risk ratings and escalation triggers.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence was fragmented, scenario calculations were repeated manually, and relationship risks could not be reduced to reliable rules.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding makes transparent scenario tools and evidence assembly cheaper to build. Bounded models can organise authorised narrative material without being trusted to predict workforce behaviour.
tasks.still_hard: Industrial action, trust and negotiating responses remain uncertain. Legal advice may require restricted handling, and historical disputes may be poor guides to current conditions.
tasks.human_edge: Judging which uncertainties matter, challenging reassuring assumptions and deciding what exposure the organisation can accept.

ambition.what: Reassess exposure whenever a bargaining option crosses an agreed escalation threshold.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends more time challenging assumptions and developing mitigations. They can trigger a fresh risk review; management retains authority to accept exposure.

reach.task: Prepare workforce contingency choices for management.
reach.learn: Operational dependencies, escalation thresholds, continuity trade-offs and consultation obligations.

evidence.claim: Transparent scenario calculations and referenced drafting can support risk assessment; the digest supplies no validated bargaining-risk prediction case.
A documented generated-report failure supports checking every material source reference.
The EU AI Act identifies specified worker-management AI applications as high-risk; intended use must be assessed.

assumptions: The assessment concerns bargaining strategies, not individual worker propensity or union activity scores.
Scenario impacts are conditional calculations, not validated forecasts of industrial action.
The supplied judgement-heavy prior fits final risk assessment; evidence assembly and calculations have greater automation potential.
Build ranges assume reuse of the bargaining baseline and scenario definitions.
unknowns: Which operational dependencies and financial assumptions are available.
Who accepts financial, operational and relationship exposure.
Whether legal advice may be processed in the proposed environment.
Applicable national consultation requirements and approved data-processing arrangements.
research_questions: Can historical scenario costs be reproduced and independently reconciled?
Which assumptions change the recommended strategy most?
Which GDPR safeguards and national rules apply to the evidence used?
Does the intended model use fall within a regulated worker-management application?
new_work: Maintain scenario assumptions and escalation thresholds.
Check references, calculations and omitted downside scenarios.
Track which assumptions proved wrong after negotiations.
Maintain evidence permissions and exclusions for restricted advice.

role.altitude: The role shifts toward earlier intervention, bargaining preparation and testing consequential assumptions. People retain responsibility for conversations, agreement interpretation and recommendations; management retains mandate and risk-acceptance decisions.
reach: Work with compensation specialists on the distribution and recurring cost of bargaining proposals.
Work with payroll staff to resolve agreement-related discrepancies before they recur.
Work with equal opportunity specialists to recognise grievances needing specialist handling.
skills_to_grow: Build and challenge transparent financial scenarios.
Translate agreement clauses into testable controls while preserving ambiguous cases.
Verify generated summaries against source documents.
Apply GDPR, relevant EU AI Act requirements and national consultation rules to intended uses.
Facilitate difficult conversations and explain uncertainty clearly.
role.ambitious_version: Provide an early labor-relations service that combines timely agreement checks, accessible facilitated conversations and rapidly refreshed bargaining scenarios, while keeping trust and consequential decisions with people.
